# Source Map — MAC-010, IMF 2022 Article IV Full Report (Mexico)

## Document frame
- **Type**: Staff report accompanying Article IV consultation; Press Release PR22/373; Informational Annex. IMF Country Report No. 22/334, November 2022. Mission discussions ended September 23, 2022; staff report completed October 18, 2022; Executive Board consideration November 2, 2022; press release November 4, 2022. (pp.1–2)
- **Accounting/basis**: Macro projections are staff estimates; figures incorporate national sources (Banxico, INEGI, SHCP, CONEVAL). General government figures exclude state/local governments and include SOEs and public development banks (p.4, Table 1 footnotes). Fiscal data shown in both GFSM 2014 and authorities' presentation (Table 2/3).
- **Attribution boundary**: Analysis and forecasts, not audited outcomes. Tables and annexes are authoritative; narrative is staff appraisal.

## Baseline macro conditions (selected indicators, % or % GDP unless noted)
- Real GDP growth: 4.8 (2021), 2.1 proj. (2022), 1.2 proj. (2023) (p.4 Table 1).
- Unemployment rate (%): 4.1 (2021), 3.4 (2022), 3.7 (2023) (p.4).
- CPI end of period (%): 7.4 (2021), 8.5 (2022), 4.8 (2023). CPI period average: 5.7, 8.0, 6.3 (p.4).
- Headline inflation ran 8.7% by August 2022, from ~3% end-2020; core inflation 8.1%; food inflation 14.1% in August, contributing >50% of excess headline inflation (p.5, ¶5).
- Fiscal balance (% GDP): −3.8 (2021), −3.8 (2022), −4.1 (2023). Gross public sector debt (% GDP): 57.6, 56.2, 57.7 (p.4).
- Current account balance (% GDP): −0.4 (2021), −1.2 (2022), −1.2 (2023). Gross int'l reserves: US$207.7bn / 205.7bn / 207.4bn; import cover 3.9/3.8/3.8 months (p.4).
- Gross fed oil revenue 2022H1: ~US$23bn+ for PEMEX (EBITDA), >2× year-earlier (p.8, ¶12).
- Poverty headcount (CONEVAL, 2020): 43.9% (p.4 Table 1).

## Policy status — enacted vs recommended
- **Enacted/operational**: Banxico policy rate at 9.25% after successive hikes (25→50→75 bp); ~6 pp above U.S. Fed; terminal market-implied ≈10.5% by Q1 2023 (p.6, ¶6; p.2 PR). Fuel price smoothing regime in force; subsidy cost ~1.5% of GDP, lowering inflation by ~2 pp (p.15, ¶23). Nonbinding agreement with food producers/distributors covering 24 items for 6 months; tariff reductions on select foods (p.7, ¶11; p.15, ¶23). 2023 draft budget approved by Congress; deficit 3.8→4.1% of GDP; neutral fiscal stance (Box 1, p.9). FEIP reserves <0.1% of GDP; minimum estimated need 0.3% of GDP (p.17, ¶29).
- **Proposed/recommended**: Staff call for additional Banxico hikes to ≥10% and firmly restrictive real ex-ante rate (>5% in 2023) (pp.13–14, ¶¶21–22). Shift to market-based fuel pricing; targeted support for vulnerable households (p.15, ¶23; p.16, ¶29). Gradual increase in productive spending financed by tax reform (p.2 PR; p.16, ¶29). FRBL reforms: well-calibrated debt anchor, broader structural spending rule, medium-term fiscal strategy, tighter escape clauses, strengthened fiscal council (p.16, ¶29). FSAP recommendations: mandatory consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates; LTV/DTI macroprudential tools; benefit-ownership register; expanded IPAB remit; enhanced ELA framework; strengthened cyber and climate-risk supervision (pp.19–20, ¶¶37–38, 41). Banxico CBDC plan (p.21, ¶40).
- **Authorities' position (stated, not adjudicated)**: fuel price stabilization aligned with pledge that prices not rise in real terms vs November 2018; willing to consider FEIP reforms enabling debt-funded stabilization reserve; expect nearshoring benefits; manufacturing less exposed to U.S. slowdown than services (¶¶27, 31, 34; Box 1 p.9; ¶18).

## Risks and quantified scenarios
- Downside risks weighted > upside; main downside: higher global inflation, tighter global financial conditions, sharper U.S. slowdown (p.10, ¶17). Illustrative global tightening/inflation scenario (Box 2, p.12): oil +10%, food +50% shock; combined with dislocated expectations and 1% domestic demand drop, output trough >2% below baseline in 2023.
- U.S.-Mexico short-term GDP elasticity >1 (Annex VII cited). Mexican potential per-capita growth recovers to "slightly above 1%" post-2024 absent major reforms (p.10, ¶16).
- Financial sector: NPLs modestly elevated; capital adequacy >19% (vs 16% pre-pandemic); FSAP stress tests confirm resilience but some smaller banks need buffers (pp.7, ¶10; p.19, ¶35). PEMEX debt high; external spreads above sovereign (p.8, ¶12).

## Fiscal framework and legal/institutional constraints
- Balanced budget rule + debt issuance constraints limit countercyclical capacity (p.16, ¶29). FEIP replenishment restricted under FRBL; debt cannot be issued for non-capital spending (p.17, fn 8). Top 20% of income distribution received ~45% of fuel excise tax benefits; bottom 20% ~6% (p.16, fn 7, citing MoF 2020). Fuel tax expenditure therefore regressive.
- AML/CFT legal framework aligned with FATF; effectiveness focus now (p.20, ¶41). 2014 Financial Groups law needs amendment to make consolidated supervision mandatory (p.20, ¶37).

## Distributional and data quality notes
- Higher minimum wage projected to rise from 42% of median formal wage (2018) to 59% (2022); real per-capita labor income up ~5% y/y by mid-2022 (p.15, ¶24).
- Data revisions/measurement: output gap estimated −2½% in early 2021; nearly closed by mid-2022 (p.5, ¶4). Reserves ARA coverage 125% (p.7, ¶8). No IMF data-quality caveat flagged in cover material.

## Source role and contrary material
- **Role**: International organization (IMF) staff appraisal; press release reflects Executive Board views. Teamed with parallel 2022 FSAP/FSSA.
- **Authorities' contrary emphasis**: Resilience, prudent frameworks, fiscal discipline, manufacturing resilience, nearshoring opportunity (¶¶18, 26, 27, 31, 34, 42).
- **Staff contrary emphasis**: Regressive untargeted subsidies, weak productivity, AML/CFT effectiveness gap, need for fiscal-framework reform, banking consolidation framework gaps (¶¶23, 24, 29, 37, 41).

## Limitations and items for stronger-model review
- Annexes I–XIV (pp.53–89 in report) referenced but not in this extract; reopen for debt sustainability (Annex III), fiscal framework (Annex X), and FSAP details (Annex XI).
- `5B.6` public investment evidence partial; reopen Annex X and Box 1 for capex composition.
- `5B.2`/`5B.5` governance: only structural indicators aggregates (p.22 chart) present; no governance-specific excerpts.
- Auditor qualifications: not applicable — this is staff analysis, not audited financial statements; treat staff projections vs authorities' views as distinct categories.
- Verify all percentages, rates, and dates against pp.4 Table 1 and Box 1 (p.9) when re-citing.

Content fit within 1200 tokens; no continuation needed.
